statement: Decode a MAX31855 SPI word to the thermocouple temperature (0.25 C per LSB, signed 14 bit) and the internal temperature (0.0625 C per LSB, signed 12 bit) as in the datasheet.
Decode a MAX6675 SPI word to the thermocouple temperature (0.25 C per LSB, 12 bit).
Report an invalid read for open circuit, short to GND, short to VCC, a missing device (all zeros or all ones) and a fault flag without a reason bit.
Build a UART frame $<temp>,<duty>*<CRC> with CRC-8 (polynomial 0x07, start value 0) that the sensor-data-logger accepts.
Refuse to build a frame for values the logger rejects (temperature outside -40..85 C, duty outside 0..100 %, NaN) or when the buffer is too small.
On/off control switches on below setpoint minus hysteresis, off above setpoint plus hysteresis, and keeps its state inside the band.
PID output is P + I + D with the derivative taken on the measurement, so a setpoint step gives no output spike.
PID integral does not grow while the output is saturated (anti-windup) and the output leaves the limit as soon as the error changes sign.
PID output always stays within its configured limits, also for very large errors.
The heater is switched off and stays off until reset when the reading reaches TEMP_CUTOFF_C (80 C).
A single bad thermocouple read switches the heater off for that sample only; SENSOR_FAULT_LIMIT (3) bad reads in a row switch it off until reset.

If the heater runs at RUNAWAY_DUTY_PCT (90 %) or more for RUNAWAY_WINDOW_S (90 s) without a rise of RUNAWAY_MIN_RISE_C (2 C), for example because the thermocouple fell off the plate, the heater is switched off until reset.
After MAX_RUN_S (1800 s) of heating the heater is switched off and stays off while logging continues.

With the PID controller on a simulated first-order plant with dead time, the temperature reaches the setpoint with no steady-state error and the output stays within limits. This checks the code, not the real heater.
The analysis script calculates the plant model, SIMC gains, rise time, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error correctly on generated curves with known answers.
The analysis script reports bad input (wrong columns, setpoint below the start value) and runs that did not settle, instead of returning numbers.
The analysis command line reads a logged CSV and writes the metrics and the plots.
The MOSFET gate is held low by a pull-down until the timer takes over, so the heater is off at reset.
The independent watchdog resets the MCU (heater off) if the control loop hangs for more than 2 s.
A fuse and a bimetal thermal switch in series with the heater switch it off independently of the firmware.
The measured open-loop, on/off and PID step responses are recorded and analysed (see README, Results).
